findings.message: A different agent (Claude) checked the work in a separate headless process.

This packet contains planning documents only and makes no implementation claims. The CI-provenance design is internally consistent on the main points: EP9-only eligibility, fixed-workflow execution, separate signing, closing-time cryptographic re-verification, latest-attempt ordering, a signed five-minute checkpoint and preservation of history. Its known gaps are stated openly, carried forward as warnings, and gated before implementation. I found no release-relevant error. Several status statements are stale or contradict each other. Some design assertions are stated more firmly than their acknowledged open issues allow.

spec.md closing note says "Scenarios and independent reviews have not been performed; no phase or implementation approval is claimed." This contradicts the ticket work log (reviews 628139a4 and 4f3dc321) and approved-planning-followthrough.md, which says review 0f3addde approved the packet and an intake review stamp was recorded. Update the note so it states that planning/intake approval exists and that implementation and qualification approval do not.

The ticket.md work log ends at review 4f3dc321 and omits d4f81dbd and the approval 0f3addde. Meanwhile the frontmatter still shows phase: intake / status: in_progress with the creation timestamp as last_modified. The authoritative ticket record trails the evidence narrative, which weakens traceability for later gates.

approved-planning-followthrough.md says 0f3addde approved "the exact current packet", but no packet digest or file manifest is recorded here. The packet now includes the follow-through file itself, so a reader cannot tell which bytes were approved. Record the approved packet identity (digest or file list with hashes) so the approval cannot be silently stretched to cover later edits.

ci-provenance-design.md flatly says that "trusted workflow structure separates execution-mode and checkpoint-mode jobs; a caller cannot relabel an arbitrary checkpoint as execution." The follow-through warning, however, notes that certificates may not identify an individual job within a workflow, so this is unproven. Until distinct predicate types or separately pinned reusable workflows are designed, mark the sentence as a requirement rather than an established property.

The latest-attempt ordering in done_when ("current execution attempt ... authenticated") depends on a candidate-to-run association that does not exist yet: workflow_dispatch head_sha identifies the workflow, not the candidate. Enumerating runs that are pending or have no artifacts is also unsolved. Both are deferred to implementation planning, but they are central to the revocation claim and should be a hard entry criterion for that phase, not just a nonblocking note.

The five-minute offline freshness check rejects a local clock that reads earlier than the signing time, but a clock held between signing and expiry keeps a checkpoint valid indefinitely. The follow-through acknowledges this honest-clock assumption, but spec.md R2 and the checkpoint scenario do not. Add it to the user-facing freshness limits so nobody over-claims.

Feasibility risks are correctly treated as blocking adoption rather than being silently relaxed: two-second closing-hook verification latency, query-to-close latency within five minutes, and GitHub runner credential isolation. Keep these as explicit go/no-go gates.
